A_target.statement: The set of [[Definition:Prime Number|prime numbers]] is [[Definition:Infinite Set|infinite]].

B_source.statement: Given any finite list of objects, one can construct a new object not on the list.

substitutions.a finite list of objects: a finite list of primes p_1,...,p_k
substitutions.the newly constructed object outside the: a prime factor of N = p_1*...*p_k + 1

derived.the new object differs from all listed o: the new prime divides N but none of the p_i do
derived.no finite list is complete: no finite list of primes is complete

validity_conditions: For any finite set of primes, N = product + 1 leaves remainder 1 when divided by each p_i, so no p_i divides N.
N > 1 has some prime factor, which is therefore not in the list.
This is the 'construct something outside any finite list' skeleton applied to primes.
proof_plan: {{AimForCont}} that $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k$ are all the primes.

For each $i$, $N \equiv 1 \pmod {p_i}$, so $p_i \nmid N$.
But $N > 1$, so by the [[Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic]] $N$ has a prime factor $p$.
